take_homes: You can't hand over an agent. Pick the smallest shape that moves one teammate's job: the context, a skill, a pushed output or a pull interface. For my team it is probably the shared context.
Accountability is the part that doesn't copy. If I can't put a name on who owns and judges the output, the people plan isn't done, however clean the technical plan looks.
Test the switch: ask what has to be true for one real person to drop what she does today. Start with one conversation, not a rollout.

monday.move: Talk to one analyst from the pricing working group about how she builds the pilot-cohort brief today. Ask where she would look for it, and test whether a fresh-data brief in that place is right the first time she opens it.
monday.who: One analyst from the pricing working group (I still need to pick the name)
monday.when: Monday morning, 30 minutes, before the next brief goes out
monday.stop_condition: If she says she wouldn't open it in the place I'd put it, or the first brief needs her to rework it, I stop and redesign the shape before involving the other thirteen.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, and I don't yet have an owner for the shared version. Both stay UNASSIGNED.

misconception.why: I came in thinking that getting good meant better prompts. The module says the agent file is a page of instructions and the value is in the memory, the corrections and the named owner. I haven't yet seen that work with my own team, so it isn't fully changed.

one_line: Short and practical: the first half walks you through it and the second half mostly says it again, but the line that a name doesn't travel in a folder is worth the hour.
